THE REMAINING OBJECTIVE IS SIMPLE:

MAKE ONE REAL OWNER-AUTHENTICATED IVX CHAT REQUEST
TRAVERSE THE COMPLETE AUTONOMOUS PIPELINE.

==================================================
P0-1 — FIX SUPABASE SERVICE ROLE RUNTIME
==================================================

Last evidence reported:

SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
→ validation returning HTTP 503

DO NOT ASK OWNER TO PASTE THE KEY.

Inspect the REAL production runtime binding.

Determine:

1. Is SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY present?
2. Which Render service owns it?
3. Does the autonomous worker receive it?
4. Is the value loaded at process startup?
5. Is the Supabase URL correct?
6. Is the 503 coming from IVX, Render, Supabase, proxy,
   health logic, or credential validation code?
7. Is this actually an invalid credential or an infrastructure failure?

Perform a REAL authenticated Supabase operation appropriate for
service-role validation.

NEVER PRINT THE SECRET.

Return:

SUPABASE KEY PRESENT:
YES / NO

BOUND TO CORRECT SERVICE:
YES / NO

AUTHENTICATED SUPABASE REQUEST:
PASS / FAIL

HTTP STATUS:

ROOT CAUSE:

If credential exists and works:
do NOT rotate it.

If credential exists but runtime cannot consume it:
FIX THE BINDING.

Only request owner intervention if a real authentication attempt
proves the credential itself is revoked/invalid.

==================================================
P0-2 — OWNER AUTHENTICATION
==================================================

The autonomous canary stopped because there was no authenticated
owner session.

DO NOT BYPASS OWNER AUTH.

DO NOT weaken authentication.

DO NOT create fake owner authorization.

Use the normal production IVX owner login/session flow.

The owner will authenticate through the actual IVX application.

<redacted identifier>

<actual production auth mechanism>

Do not expose passwords, tokens, cookies, JWTs or secrets.

==================================================
P0-3 — OWNER APPROVAL ONCE
==================================================

From the authenticated production IVX IA Chat, submit ONE harmless
engineering canary.

Use a uniquely identifiable, reversible change.

IVX may ask owner authorization ONCE.

After owner presses YES:

persist authorization against that task/scope.

Required:

OWNER APPROVAL COUNT = 1

Retries must reuse that authorization.

==================================================

==================================================

<real>

<real>

<real>

PASS

PASS

STOP.

Trace and FIX the exact broken arrow:

CHAT
→ INTENT

→ CREATE TASK

Then retry through IVX.

==================================================
P0-5 — PROVE REAL WORKER EXECUTION
==================================================

→ QUEUED
→ CLAIMED
→ INSPECTING
→ IMPLEMENTING
→ TESTING
→ COMMITTING
→ PUSHING
→ DEPLOYING
→ VERIFYING
→ COMPLETED

Every status must originate from actual backend/worker state.

NO LLM-generated fake progress.

NO invented percentages.

NO Rork simulation.

==================================================
P0-6 — RORK MUST NOT IMPLEMENT THE CANARY
==================================================

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Rork may:

inspect
observe
QA
diagnose infrastructure failure

Rork MUST NOT manually make the canary source-code change.

The IVX autonomous developer must perform:

repository read
file modification
diff
tests
commit
push
deployment
production verification

If Rork manually performs the canary:

FINAL AUTONOMOUS TEST = INVALID.
